headline: On a flat, real button `StyleX` and the two next-yak 9.7 paths tie the fastest cluster at ~0.44-0.53 ms/1k SSR; folding erases the `Yak` wrapper entirely, and `emotion`'s `murmur2` hash is the single most expensive styling function in the run.

microbench.why: On flat depth-1 JSX there is nothing to compose away, so the win is whoever ships zero render-time styling. `StyleX` reads a compiled atomic style object at 0.444 ms/1k, the styled perf runtime folds `<DenseButton>` to `<button className>` at 0.479, the css-prop path 0.534. Turning folding off (`next-yak-9.7-nofold`, 0.962 ms/1k) doubles the cost as the `Yak` wrapper returns and renders per button. The hashers trail, `styled-components` 1.21 ms/1k, `goober` 1.31, `emotion` 2.86.

autocannon.why: Serving the button under load, the styled perf runtime's folded flat markup leads at 596 req/s with the css-prop path at 575. `StyleX` and `vanilla` sit at 462-473 req/s, a step back because their markup carries more class bytes per element. The hashers land far behind as each request re-serializes, `styled-components` 270, `emotion` 131.

attribution.why: `StyleX`, the css-prop fold and the styled perf runtime cluster at 1.32-1.37 ms with library slices at or near zero (styled perf 0.152 ms, css-prop 0.153, `StyleX` 0). Folding does the work: `next-yak-9.7-nofold` pays 0.786 ms of library time for the returned `Yak` wrapper and rises to 2.63 ms. `emotion` spends 4.27 ms of 7.53 ms in `murmur2`, `styled-components` 1.45 ms in `generateAndInjectStyles`.

hydrate.why: The static-class lanes hydrate identically at ~59.6-59.8 ms, a tie inside the sampling spread, because a single button carries a trivial component tree. The runtime hashers inject and reflow, `emotion` 119 ms, `goober` 162 ms, `styled-components` 162 ms.

inp.why: Toggling the button re-renders one element in ~7.00 ms across every static-class lane, a statistical tie. The hashers re-inject on the interaction, `goober` 16.5 ms, `styled-components` 17.0 ms, `emotion` 29.3 ms.

mount.why: Cold-mounting one button parses a small static sheet, so `StyleX`, `vanilla` and both folded next-yak paths land at 111-113 ms. The runtime libraries pay first-inject, `goober` 160 ms, `styled-components` 161 ms, `emotion` 185 ms.

renderTiming.why: One recalc for every lane; a single button paints the same way regardless of technique. The styleMs difference between the two `StyleX` builds (`@layer` 0.382 ms vs the `:not()` twin 0.674) reflects selector-matching cost in the engine, not recalc count.

payload.why: The css-prop fold ships the least at 3.95 kB gzipped, under `vanilla` (4.44 kB); the styled perf runtime carries its wrapper runtime at 4.90 kB. `StyleX` adds 9.10 kB of atomic classes and the hashers 16-17 kB, `styled-components` 17.2 kB, `emotion` 16.7 kB, `panda` 16.1 kB.

nsweep.why: The flat button never composes, so the styled perf runtime, `StyleX`, `vanilla` and the css-prop path scale together at 4.84-5.12 ms for 4000 buttons. `next-yak-9.7-nofold` doubles to 10.0 ms as the `Yak` wrapper renders per button; the hashers reach `styled-components` 12.9 ms, `emotion` 29.8 ms.

crossCase: `realistic-button` is the depth-1 anchor of the composition ladder (`compose-1`, `compose-3`, `compose-6` below). Here folding, not the perf runtime, is the whole win: it deletes the styling component so the styled path ties the extracted floor, and switching folding off doubles the SSR cost. Under composition the split reverses, and the perf runtime carries the load while folding leaves a residual wrapper.
